questions.question: Which language should the frontend use?
questions.rationale: TypeScript is a strong default for a maintainable interactive frontend.

options.label: TypeScript
options.description: Typed JavaScript for safer UI and graph interactions.

options.label: JavaScript
options.description: Plain JavaScript with no static type annotations.

questions.question: Which framework should the frontend use?
questions.rationale: React is the default component framework for this project-planning workflow.

options.label: React
options.description: Component-based UI with a broad ecosystem.

options.label: Plain HTML
options.description: A lightweight frontend without a component framework.

questions.question: Which existing behaviors and interactions must the frontend preserve?
questions.answer: Preserve all existing app behavior: multiline link editor, analyze, local text-file import, demo and clear actions, server/link summary, critical-server list, failure impact breakdown, graph highlighting, and click-to-view impact.
questions.rationale: These behaviors are present in the existing Tkinter application and the request asks to modernize its frontend.
questions.recommendedChoice: Preserve all existing app behavior: multiline link editor, analyze, local text-file import, demo and clear actions, server/link summary, critical-server list, failure impact breakdown, graph highlighting, and click-to-view impact.

questions.question: Which data stores does the application need?
questions.rationale: The graph is analyzed in memory; file loading reads a user-selected local text file and no cloud persistence is present.

options.label: No datastore required
options.description: The application does not persist data.

options.label: PostgreSQL
options.description: Relational database for persistent application data.

options.label: Azure Blob Storage
options.description: Object storage for files and media.

questions.question: Do users need to sign in to use application features?
questions.rationale: The existing standalone tool has no user accounts or authenticated API features.

options.label: No
options.description: The application is available without user sign-in.

options.label: Yes
options.description: Users must sign in to use application features.
